correctness.rationale: The four angular samples on each circle give the exact mean, first harmonic and one real second harmonic projection. Independent radii remove the first-harmonic unknowns; non-right-angle twist removes the second harmonic. The sole remaining Hermitian null direction is diag(r^2s^2,-r^2-s^2,1), with nonzero determinant for r,s>0, excluding rank-at-most-two signal differences. Explicit polynomials show failure on each forbidden locus; an odd cubic determinant argument gives the sharp seven-measurement lower bound. The embedded symbolic checker confirms a Gaussian-integer sample and degenerate cases; the all-parameter assertion is analytically proved.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural parameter-space classification of a balanced minimal-cardinality concentric sampling family, motivated by prior two-circle phase retrieval. It identifies precisely how discrete second-harmonic aliasing destroys identifiability at right-angle twists, and why radial separation restores all first-harmonic information. This is not a single arbitrary example or a trivial rephrasing of the known eight-sample benchmark.
